claim_boundary.supports: Kernel-checked for modules over a field: with d1 d0 = 0 the sequence 0 -> H1 -> Q1 -> im d1 -> 0 is exact (injective, ker = range, onto) and, in finite dimension, dim Q1 = dim H1 + dim im d1 and dim Q1 + dim im d0 = dim C1. When H1 and im d1 are both nontrivial NO section is invariant under the automorphisms 1 + incl f pi of the extension (these act simply transitively on the sections and are automorphisms of the extension, not of the window and not isometries of J; INSTANCE model C1 = Q^2, d0 = 0, d1(a,b) = b); when H1 or im d1 is trivial (and pi is onto) there is exactly one section and it is invariant (exists_unique_invariant_section_of_trivial). Exactly one diagnostic class holds for every (Phi1, Gamma2); for a definite J, Phi1 = 0 iff the class is zero (false for a seminorm, kernel instance with J = 0 on Q). For d1 d0 = 0 and an attained minimum Phi1, ||d1 h||_1 <= c Phi1 whenever sum_r |d1_re| <= c w_e for all e (gamma_le_opnorm_phi, with gamma2_repair moving from the representative to the minimiser); at the minimiser itself the bound needs no closure (gamma_at_minimiser_le). The operator bound ||d1 v||_1 <= c ||v||_J for all v is equivalent to these column inequalities (opbound_of_columns, columns_of_opbound), so the least c is max_e column sum / w_e when all w_e > 0 (that max formula and its null-weight convention are the checker definition); a smaller constant fails (kernel instance with the largest entry as c). Native table over 14 windows with a verified primal potential and dual vector each (cost(x) = y.h = Phi1, d0^T y = 0, |y_e| <= w_e), dim H1 recomputed in the checker from an explicit nullspace basis of d1 minus rank d0, splitting freedom dim H1 * dim im d1, class, operator norm and inequality. One window has d1 d0 != 0: there kappa1 is undefined and the representative norm ||d1 h||_1 = 2 exceeds ||d1|| Phi1 = 0, but the source Gamma2 at the minimal residual h* = 0 is 0 and the inequality holds, so Gamma2 is withheld for it. For a seminorm (a zero-weight edge) the label ExactClass means only Phi1 = 0: seminorm_zero_weight_filled has Phi1 = 0 and ||d1 h||_1 = 1.
claim_boundary.does_not_support: Any derivation of the window; norms other than weighted L1 for the inequality; complex coefficients; a statement that the sequence has or lacks a section natural for automorphisms of the window (graph automorphisms preserving d0, d1 and the weights); the converse "if there is an invariant section then dim H1 * dim im d1 = 0" is native by dimension (section_dim) with the trivial-factor halves in the kernel; existence of minimisers for general norms; Phi1 >= 0 as a theorem for the weighted-L1 window (gamma2_nonneg is anchored, Phi1 >= 0 needs the cost bridge of the degree-1 window node); any physical reading of the classes.
claim_boundary.narrowest_claim: For a window over a field with d1 d0 = 0 the sequence 0 -> H1 -> Q1 -> im d1 -> 0 is exact; no section is invariant under 1 + incl f pi when dim H1 > 0 and dim im d1 > 0 (kernel), and when dim H1 * dim im d1 = 0 there is exactly one section and it is invariant (kernel); every class has exactly one diagnostic class; Phi1 = 0 iff the class is zero for a definite J; and ||d1 h||_1 <= c Phi1 for an attained minimum and c at least the J-to-L1 column bound.
claim_boundary.next_test: Decide the splitting claim for the finite group G of automorphisms of the K4 two-face window (graph automorphisms preserving the two faces, d0, d1 and the weights) by solving the linear fixed-point equations of G on the affine section space over Hom(im d1, H1) = Q^2: either a G-fixed section exists or the fixed locus is empty.

second_review.notes: Cold read of run 20261021T175809Z_staged; I recompiled WdpQuotientSequence.lean (exit 0; axioms propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound, diag_unique propext / Quot.sound). Anchors checked against their statements: exact_sequence (incl injective, ker pi = range incl, pi onto) and finrank_sequence are general over a field with d1 d0 = 0 as an explicit hypothesis; no_natural_section is the dual-functional argument and is correct (hypotheses Nontrivial H, Nontrivial I, injective i, exact p); exists_unique_invariant_section_of_trivial now covers both boundary halves (H trivial: p injective hence an equivalence; I trivial: the zero section) and takes surjectivity of p as a hypothesis, so the earlier gap (existence, and the d1 = 0 case, were claimed but not in Lean) is closed; isPhi_zero_iff needs only J >= 0 and J v = 0 iff v = 0; opbound_of_columns / columns_of_opbound are the column-sum equivalence; gamma_le_opnorm_phi uses hcl and IsPhiM and gamma2_repair; gamma_at_minimiser_le needs no closure. The checker now recomputes dim H1 from an explicit RREF nullspace of d1 (each vector checked killed by d1, basis checked independent) minus rank d0, uses the dual-LP Phi1 with exact primal/dual witness verification, withholds Gamma2 and sets diag = NotAWindow when d1 d0 != 0, and the 14 ids are fixed. I read the public windows: violates_d1d0_edge is nv=2, one edge, d1 = (1), h = 2 (Phi1 = 0, representative norm 2, minimal residual 0 has Gamma2 0), exactly as the profile says; seminorm_zero_weight_filled has Phi1 = 0, Gamma2 = 1, label ExactClass, documented. Earlier pass (a): all eight amendments are in the final text and files (Gamma2 convention with gamma2_repair / gamma_at_minimiser_le, column-form wording with the max formula marked as the checker definition, extension-automorphism wording, narrowest_claim, does_not_support additions, seminorm sentence, next_test as a fixed-locus computation, NoRule -> NotAWindow, gamma2_repair and gamma2_nonneg added as anchors); the mutants now include no-splitting-for-d1-zero, both Gamma2-reading mutants, and the seminorm relabel (14 semantic mutants). (b) No weakened check; the rebuild is an improvement. (c) Residual issues: (1) supports says the automorphisms 1 + incl f pi 'act simply transitively on the sections'; Lean proves freeness (phi_section_iff: phi_f fixes a section iff f = 0) and that phi_f maps sections to sections (phi_induces_id), but transitivity (any two sections differ by some f) is not formalised. The statement is true but sits in a sentence that opens 'Kernel-checked'. (2) gamma_at_minimiser_le is existential (exists x with gamma2 (h + D0 x) <= c p); supports says 'at the minimiser itself the bound needs no closure'. The proof works for every minimiser, but the stated theorem only gives some minimiser, and the source takes Gamma2 at a particular computed minimal residual (non-unique in general for L1). The claim is true as an existence statement; it should say 'at some (indeed every, by the same proof) minimiser' or the Lean statement should be made universal. I treat this as an amendment, not a rebuild, because a text fix makes the claim exact. (3) narrowest_claim 'every class has exactly one diagnostic class' is stronger than diag_unique, which is a statement about a pair of rationals (phi, gam); that Phi1 and Gamma2 are functions of the class [h] is definitional for Phi1 and is gamma2_repair (matrix form, closure needed) for Gamma2; the module-level IsPhi / Q1 and the matrix-level gamma2 are not linked in one Lean statement. (4) narrowest_claim opens 'For a window over a field' but its last conjunct (||d1 h||_1 <= c Phi1) is a statement over Q with Fin-indexed matrices; sequence results are field-general, the inequality is not. (5) does_not_support contains a garbled clause: it lists as unsupported 'the converse if there is an invariant section then dim H1 * dim im d1 = 0 ... is native by dimension with the trivial-factor halves in the kernel', but that converse IS the contrapositive of no_natural_section in the kernel (once dim > 0 is identified with Nontrivial); what is native is only the finrank product section_dim and the canonical_split flag. (6) Leaves exact_dims (rank-nullity between two elimination routines), classes_hit (always 1) and dim_im (= rank_d1) are redundant and are not evidence for the claim; the claim does not rely on them. (7) The checker fixes the 14 windows by id; contents are bound by the stage digest (not exploitable here). (8) DAG: with the earlier suggested narrowing the statement is fully backed by the Lean anchors, so I would keep PROVED_LEAN for the narrowed statement rather than lowering to CONDITIONAL; if the unqualified 'no canonical splitting' or 'Phi1 >= 0' is retained the status should be CONDITIONAL.
amendments: supports: replace 'these act simply transitively on the sections' by 'these act freely on the sections (phi_section_iff) and map sections to sections; transitivity is not formalised'.

dag_suggestion.statement: For a window over a field with d1 d0 = 0, kappa1 is well defined on Q1 and 0 -> H1 -> Q1 -> im d1 -> 0 is exact with dim Q1 = dim H1 + dim im d1; when dim H1 > 0 and dim im d1 > 0 no section is invariant under the automorphisms 1 + incl f pi of the extension (which act freely on the sections and are not automorphisms of the window), and when either vanishes the section is unique and invariant; every pair (Phi1, Gamma2) lies in exactly one diagnostic class; for a definite J, Phi1 = 0 iff the class of h is zero (false for a seminorm); and for weighted L1 over Q with an attained minimum, ||d1 h||_1 <= c Phi1 whenever c is at least the largest column-sum-to-weight ratio (equivalent to the operator bound). Naturality of the splitting for automorphisms of the window, other norms, complex coefficients and Phi1 >= 0 are not covered.
dag_suggestion.status: PROVED_LEAN (for the narrowed statement; CONDITIONAL if the unqualified 'no canonical splitting' or 'Phi1 >= 0' is retained)
dag_suggestion.bottleneck: 'No canonical splitting' is proved only for the unipotent automorphisms of the extension (a torsor statement) and is false for dim H1 = 0 or d1 = 0; Gamma2 is the representative norm (equal to the source value at the minimal residual when d1 d0 = 0); the norm hypothesis and an attained minimiser are assumed; naturality for window automorphisms is the node's next test.

earlier_pass.notes: Lean: exact_sequence, finrank_sequence, no_natural_section (the dual-functional argument is correct over any field), phi_section_iff, isPhi_zero_iff (needs only J >= 0 and J v = 0 iff v = 0), opbound_of_columns / columns_of_opbound and gamma_le_opnorm_phi are sound and state what the profile says, with the hypotheses visible (d1 d0 = 0 as hcl, attained minimum IsPhiM). The checker computes Phi1 by dual LP against a primal producer and the class test by augmented ranks, and several theorem-level checks (Phi1 = 0 iff zero class when all weights positive; Gamma2 <= opnorm * Phi1) are genuine cross-checks of two independent computations. Problems. (1) Gamma2 convention again: gamma2 D1 v is the norm at the given vector, and gamma_le_opnorm_phi concludes gamma2 D1 h <= c * p only by moving from h to the minimiser through gamma2_repair (which needs d1 d0 = 0; gamma2_repair is not an anchor). The source quantity is the norm of d1 at the minimal residual (run.rs 169-171). Applied to the minimiser, the inequality needs no closure at all (opbound_of_columns on h*). So the table window violates_d1d0_edge (Phi1 = 0, 'Gamma2 = 2', bound_holds false) and the supports clause 'including a window with d1 d0 != 0 where the inequality fails' exhibit a convention artefact: the source Gamma2 of that window is 0 (h* = 0) and the inequality holds. The mutant bound_claimed_without_complex ('the inequality needs d1 d0 = 0') inherits the same issue. (2) Tautological leaf: dim_h1 is computed as m - r1 - r0 and exact_dims as (m - r0 == dim_h1 + r1), identically true when complex; the theorem-level check 'exact_sequence_dimensions' therefore asserts nothing, and the 'dimension count of the exact sequence' is not recomputed (no independent kernel of kappa1: no explicit nullspace of d1 modulo im d0). classes_hit is likewise always 1 because Phi1, Gamma2 >= 0. (3) 'No canonical splitting' scope: the automorphisms 1 + incl f pi are automorphisms of the abstract extension; they act simply transitively on the section space (phi_section_iff), so 'no invariant section' is the torsor statement, and they are not automorphisms of the window (graph/weights) or isometries for J. The claim boundary does say 'unipotent group only', but the supports label '(no canonical splitting ...)' and the DAG phrase read as a statement about the window. Also, the converse used by the table and narrowest_claim ('exactly when dim H1 > 0 and dim im d1 > 0') has only one half in Lean: section_unique_of_subsingleton proves uniqueness (not existence) of a section for H = 0 and nothing covers im d1 = 0 (d1 = 0), although the Lean docstring and relation text say 'as it is for d1 = 0'; canonical_split = (section_dim == 0) is the author's definition. (4) supports 'Gamma2 <= c Phi1 whenever the column bound ... holds' omits d1 d0 = 0 and the attained minimiser; 'so ||d1|| = max_e (sum_r |d1_re|)/w_e' is not a theorem (Lean gives the equivalence of the operator bound with the column inequalities for a given c; the max formula, with its null-weight convention, is the checker's definition). (5) seminorm_zero_weight_filled has Phi1 = 0 and Gamma2 = 1 but diag 'ExactClass' (the label follows Phi1 = 0), contradicting the source meaning of the exact class (an exact coboundary has Gamma2 = 0); the claim 'exactly one diagnostic class' is true but the label is misleading for seminorms; and the Lean seminorm_instance is J = 0 on Q with d0 = 0, not a graph window (the zero-weight graph windows are native only). (6) diag = 'NoRule' for the non-window repeats the routing/status name in a diagnostic field (Lean's own Diag type has only exact / closedResidual / active). (7) The DAG statement includes 'Phi1, Gamma2 >= 0', which is not an anchor (gamma2_nonneg exists but is not listed; Phi1 >= 0 needs J >= 0 and has no theorem). Mutants: ten genuine misreadings, but they miss the explicit boundary the claim boundary names (d1 = 0: tri_unfilled_closed has dim H1 = 1, dim im d1 = 0, unique section, canonical true; no mutant claims 'no canonical splitting' there), the Gamma2-at-minimiser reading, and the label of the seminorm-filled window. next_test is node-owned and concrete, but 'enumerating the stabiliser action on the section space' is wrong in kind: the section space is an affine space over Hom(im d1, H1) = Q^2, so the test is to solve for the fixed locus of a finite group action (linear equations over Q), and the group must be the automorphisms of the window preserving d0, d1 and the weights, not all graph automorphisms of K4. DAG: the unqualified clause 'no canonical splitting' is false for dim H1 = 0 or d1 = 0 and unproved for window automorphisms; 'Phi1 = 0 exactly for ExactClass' needs J definite; the ratio bound needs the column-sum norm, closure (for the representative form) and an attained minimum.
